probes.query: I run the push-to-Git-remote command with no bookmark or revision arguments at all. Which of my local bookmarks get pushed, where is that default selection defined, and where is it applied?

probes.query: When I push a bookmark, how does jj make sure it does not overwrite something a teammate pushed to that same remote branch after my last fetch? Which layers supply the expected remote value and which one enforces it?

probes.query: If two jj processes commit against the same repository at the same moment, so that the operation history forks, what reconciles the fork the next time the repository is opened, and what makes that safe against a third concurrent process?
expectedFacts: RepoLoader::load_at_head calls resolve_op_heads; with a single head it is used directly, otherwise resolve_op_heads takes the op-heads store lock and re-reads the heads.
Heads that are ancestors of other heads are filtered out via dag_walk_async::heads; if multiple remain, a resolver closure creates a merge operation described as 'reconcile divergent operations'.

merge_operations merges the views of the heads using closest common ancestor operations and rebases descendants; the lock is taken only so concurrent processes do not each produce another set of divergent heads.

probes.query: How does jj notice that the files on disk were last synced to an older repository state than the current one, and what exactly decides between 'needs recovery', 'just reload', and 'fine'?
expectedFacts: check_stale compares the working copy's recorded operation id with the repo's; if equal it is Fresh, otherwise it finds the closest common ancestor operation.

If the repo operation is itself the ancestor, the working copy was updated later and the repo is reloaded at the working copy's operation (Updated); if the working copy's operation is the ancestor the copy is stale unless its tree equals the working-copy commit's tree (then Fresh); otherwise it is a SiblingOperation.

handle_stale_working_copy in the CLI turns WorkingCopyStale into an error telling the user to run 'jj workspace update-stale', and SiblingOperation into an internal error suggesting 'jj op integrate'.

probes.query: When commits are rebased and one ends up with no changes, where does jj decide whether to drop it, and which commits are never dropped?

EmptyBehavior::AbandonNewlyEmpty abandons only commits that become empty and were not empty before; AbandonAllEmpty abandons all empty commits; Keep never abandons (the default).
Abandoning only happens when there is exactly one new parent, so merge commits are never abandoned; when the parent trees are unchanged, was_empty is set true as an optimization.

probes.query: When reconciling divergent commits, the merge base comes from a value that several earlier commits could have produced. How does jj pick which of those commits to use as the base, in what priority order?
expectedFacts: If exactly one commit produced the dominator value it is used directly.
Otherwise the choice is the minimum of the key (change offset, input position, negated committer timestamp in ms, commit id).

That means the lowest change offset (hidden commits without an offset count as maximum) wins, then earlier position in the caller's input order, then the more recent committer timestamp, then commit id as the final tie-break.

probes.query: Several color rules in the configuration can match the same piece of output, for example one keyed on a single label and another on a label combination. How does jj decide which style wins and how are they combined?
expectedFacts: Rules come from the [colors] table; each key is a space-separated list of labels that must appear in order (as a subsequence) within the current label stack.
Matches are ranked by the reversed list of matched label indices compared lexicographically, so a rule matching later (innermost) labels, such as 'a d' vs 'd' or 'a b c', takes precedence.

All matching styles are sorted by that priority and merged in ascending order, so higher-priority rules override individual attributes while unset attributes from lower rules remain; results are cached per label stack.

probes.query: I fetch with several branch patterns and one of the requested branches no longer exists on the remote. How does the fetch logic keep going for the rest, and what happens to my stale remote-tracking copy of the missing branch?
expectedFacts: GitFetch::fetch loops: it runs git fetch, and if git reports a missing remote ref (GitFetchStatus::NoRemoteRef), it removes that refspec from the list and retries with the remaining refspecs.
For each failed refs/heads/<name> it records '<remote>/<name>' in branches_to_prune, because git does not prune on a missing-ref failure even with --prune.
After the loop, spawn_branch_prune deletes those remote-tracking branches with 'git branch --remotes --delete'.
